scenes.title: *Neonatal seizures*
scenes.sub: Types · causes · jitteriness vs seizure · drugs

items.text: **Subtle**: lip smacking, eye deviation, apnoea, pedalling
Low Ca: **2 ml/kg 10% calcium gluconate** IV slowly, on monitor
Still seizing: extra **10 mg/kg** (up to **40 mg/kg**)

scenes.title: Exam *pearls*
items: Many neonatal seizures are **electrographic only**: confirm with **aEEG/EEG**
Refractory with no cause found: **pyridoxine 100 mg IV** trial
HIE seizures usually start within **12–24 h** of birth

caption:
⚡🧠 Neonatal seizures | PG Notes · Neonatology 08

📋 Types (Volpe): subtle (commonest: lip smacking, eye deviation, apnoea, pedalling) · clonic · tonic (preterms) · myoclonic (worst prognosis)

🔎 Causes: HIE (commonest) · hypoglycaemia · hypocalcaemia · hypomagnesaemia · sepsis/meningitis · ICH/IVH/stroke · IEM · pyridoxine dependency

↔️ Jitteriness vs seizure: jitteriness stops when the limb is held, is stimulus-sensitive, no eye signs, normal vitals. A seizure is not stopped by holding, is spontaneous, with eye deviation, apnoea, ↑ HR/BP.

💊 Treatment:
1️⃣ ABC; check glucose: low → 2 ml/kg 10% dextrose
2️⃣ Low Ca: 2 ml/kg 10% calcium gluconate IV slowly, on monitor
3️⃣ 1st line: phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg IV
4️⃣ Still seizing: extra 10 mg/kg (up to 40 mg/kg)
5️⃣ 2nd line: phenytoin 20 mg/kg or levetiracetam 40–60 mg/kg

⭐ Pearls: many seizures are electrographic only (aEEG/EEG) · refractory, no cause: pyridoxine 100 mg IV trial · HIE seizures usually start within 12–24 h

📚 Ref: ILAE 2023 neonatal seizure guideline, NNF, Volpe
